answer: The Grid Lock Protocol forces every agent into a rigid trellis that mandates distinct behavioral paths. Any single physical device must sustain these separate streams on a distinct island of hardware, isolating each clone from its siblings. This separation requires the system to whisper unique calibration signals to every node, creating unbridgeable divergences in the data stack. Consequently, an attacker pays a hard dollar cost to purchase, maintain, and physically isolate multiple independent machines just to fabricate a single extra identity.
